Section 302 Cr.P.C., for substitution of legal representatives/LRs of respondent no. 2 was moved

"*** 11. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chand Devi Daga & Ors. v. Manju K. Huma &
Ors., after examining Sections 256 and 302 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC)
and the earlier case laws, observed that LRs of a deceased complainant may be
substituted to continue complaints, regardless of whether the matter pertains to a
summons case or a warrant case. The Court emphasized that justice should not be
impeded by the complainant's death.
12. Regarding the contention that LRs must possess personal knowledge of the case,
A.C. Narayanan (supra) does not support this argument. The Court in A.C.
Narayanan was concerned with whether a power of attorney holder could file a
complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, stipulating that such
a person must have transaction knowledge to testify as a witness. Importantly, this
decision does not establish a restriction that prohibits LRs of a deceased complainant
from continuing proceedings. It emphasizes only that a power of attorney holder with
no knowledge of the facts cannot act as a witness.
13. The facts of A.C. Narayanan pertain specifically to negotiable instruments cases
and are limited to situations where a witness must have knowledge to testify. This
precedent, in opinion of this court, does not interfere with the principle that
ABHISHEK GOYAL GOYAL 2026.06.29 16:06:31 +0530 legal heirs may continue
prosecution of criminal cases. The Court further notes that criminal law aims to
punish offenders and uphold justice, independent of the complainant's continued
presence.
14. In the present case, the affidavits submitted by the LRs affirm that they are
acquainted with the facts of the case, which satisfies the competency requirement to
proceed. Their level of knowledge will determine their credibility as witnesses if
examined, but does not affect their right to pursue the complaint. They may also
produce other witnesses with knowledge of the facts to support the prosecution.
15. In conclusion, the Court finds that A.C. Narayanan does not bar LRs from
continuing complaints, and therefore the objection raised by accused no. 1 and
accused No. 2 is legally unsound. The Hon'ble Supreme Court's judgment in Chand
Devi Daga confirms that LRs can continue criminal complaints without requiring
intimate knowledge of the facts, ensuring that justice is not thwarted by
technicalities.
16. Accordingly, the application for substitution of the LRs of the deceased
complainant is allowed. However, it is clarified by the LRs of the complainant as to
who will be prosecuting the present complaint on behalf of the rest of the LRs and
